title: nexus.io.a2a
description: A2A (Agent2Agent) serve transport. Every key here is read by parseConfig in plugins/io/a2a/config.go; the auth block is parsed by pkg/nexusauth, shared with cmd/nexus-broker and nexus.io.agui.

bind.description: host:port the HTTP listener binds to. Default 127.0.0.1:8091 (loopback), so the A2A endpoint is not network-exposed without explicit opt-in. An empty string falls back to the default.

public_url.description: Absolute base URL advertised in the Agent Card's supportedInterfaces, e.g. https://agent.example.com. Defaults to http://<bind>, which is correct for the loopback default and wrong the moment a reverse proxy is involved.

jsonrpc_path.description: Absolute path the JSON-RPC 2.0 binding is mounted at. Default /a2a. Must differ from rest_prefix.

rest_prefix.description: Absolute path prefix the HTTP+JSON/REST binding is mounted under; operation paths from A2A specification section 11.3 hang off it. Default /a2a/v1. Must differ from jsonrpc_path.

strict_version_header.description: How an absent A2A-Version service parameter is read. Default false: assume 1.0, the only version this listener has ever served. true restores the literal specification section 3.6.2 reading (absent means 0.3), which this codec does not speak and therefore rejects with VersionNotSupportedError.

card_requires_auth.description: Whether GET /.well-known/agent-card.json is gated by the validator chain. Default false: the card is the pre-authentication bootstrap document a client fetches to learn which credentials to obtain (specification sections 7.3 and 8.2), and the listener binds loopback by default. Set true only when bind is network-exposed and the card must be distributed out-of-band instead.

cors_origins.description: Allowed CORS origins. A YAML list, or a single comma-separated string. A lone "*" echoes any request Origin. Empty means no CORS header at all (same-origin only).

bearer_token.description: Inline bearer token, desugared into a one-entry static validator. Takes precedence over bearer_token_env. Mutually exclusive with auth — that conflict is enforced in parseConfig, which owns the operator-facing message; it is deliberately NOT duplicated here so the two enforcement points cannot drift.

bearer_token_env.description: Name of an environment variable holding the bearer token. Consulted only when bearer_token is empty. Mutually exclusive with auth (see bearer_token).

card_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding a complete A2A Agent Card. Expanded through engine.ExpandPath, so ~ works. Mutually exclusive with card. Its supportedInterfaces, capabilities, securitySchemes and securityRequirements are ignored and overwritten from the live listener configuration.

tasks.description: Durable task store (session-scoped SQLite, <session>/plugins/nexus.io.a2a/store.db): retention plus the interruption deadline. Retention is load-bearing rather than housekeeping: a task carries its full status history, its artifacts and its message references, so an unbounded store grows with traffic rather than with the conversation. Both knobs are enforced together — a task is evicted when it exceeds either.

ttl.description: How long a TERMINAL task is kept after its last transition. Default 24h. "0s" disables age-based eviction and keeps tasks for the life of the session. Only terminal tasks are evictable; a live task is never dropped mid-turn.

max_per_context.description: How many tasks are kept per (principal, contextId) pair. Default 200. 0 disables the cap. Non-terminal tasks count against it but are never the ones evicted, so a wedged in-flight task shows up as retention pressure rather than exempting itself.

input_timeout.description: How long a task may stay parked at TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED waiting for a client to answer the agent's question. Default 15m — long enough for a human to be paged and reply, short enough that an abandoned question does not pin this listener's single agent loop. On expiry the task is failed and hitl.cancel unblocks the waiting agent. "0s" disables the deadline and lets a task stay parked until the process exits.

card.description: The hand-authored half of the Agent Card. Deliberately has no keys for interfaces, capabilities or security: those describe what the listener actually does and are derived, so an operator cannot state one that is false. Skills are hand-authored on purpose — the card is a public contract that must not track the internal tool catalog. Exactly one of card or card_file is required.

name.description: Human-readable agent name. Required by the A2A specification.

description.description: Human-readable summary of what the agent does. Required by the A2A specification.

version.description: The agent's own version, independent of the A2A protocol version.

documentation_url.description: URL of human-readable documentation for the agent.

icon_url.description: URL of an icon representing the agent.

default_input_modes.description: Media types the agent accepts when a skill does not narrow them, e.g. text/plain.

default_output_modes.description: Media types the agent produces when a skill does not narrow them.

skills.description: At least one skill. The A2A specification requires a non-empty skills list, and this plugin will not synthesize one.

id.description: Unique skill id within the card.

examples.description: Sample prompts that exercise the skill.

auth.description: Validator-chain block, parsed by pkg/nexusauth.ChainFromMap — the same parser the session broker uses. `validators` is its only key: `admin_scope` is broker-only and is rejected here. Writing `auth:` with no value is the same as omitting it.

validators.description: Validators to try, in order; the first that accepts wins. Absent, null or empty means authentication is disabled.

validator.description: One validators[] entry. The per-type keys are described by the if/then branches below rather than by one flat property list, because additionalProperties only sees properties declared in the same schema object — a flat list would have to allow every type's keys on every type, which is exactly the silent-typo hole this schema exists to close.

staticValidator.description: type: static — a table of shared bearer tokens, compared in constant time.

principal_claim.description: Accepted and ignored: a static token carries no claim set.

tokens.description: At least one entry. Duplicate token values are a config error, not last-one-wins.

principal.description: The principal id a request presenting this token acts as. Must be non-empty — an empty id behaves as a wildcard in ownership checks.

scopes.description: Optional granted scopes. A string is split on whitespace; a list is taken verbatim.

jwksValidator.description: type: jwks — OIDC JWTs verified against the issuer's published key set. Generic OIDC: no provider-specific defaults, so principal_claim has no fallback guess.

principal_claim.description: Required: the claim that becomes Principal.ID.

tenant_claim.description: Optional: the claim that becomes Principal.Tenant.

scopes_claim.description: Optional: the claim that becomes Principal.Scopes.

issuer.description: The exact value the token's iss claim must carry. Compared as an opaque string, trailing slash included.

jwks_url.description: The issuer's JWKS endpoint. Must be absolute https, except to a loopback host.

audience.description: Acceptable aud values; a token carrying any of them passes. A lone string is one audience and is not split on whitespace.

algorithms.description: Accepted JWS algorithms. Default ["RS256"]. Asymmetric only — `none` and the HMAC family are not configurable at all.

cache_ttl.description: How long a fetched key set is fresh. Default 10m.

negative_cache_ttl.description: How long an unresolvable kid is remembered, and the minimum interval between on-demand fetches. Default 1m.

http_timeout.description: Bounds a single JWKS request. Default 5s.

clock_skew.description: Leeway applied to exp and nbf. Default 1m, capped at 5m.

introspectValidator.description: type: introspect — opaque tokens verified by calling the issuer's RFC 7662 introspection endpoint.

principal_claim.description: Required: the claim that becomes Principal.ID.

tenant_claim.description: Optional: the claim that becomes Principal.Tenant.

scopes_claim.description: Optional: the claim that becomes Principal.Scopes.

introspection_url.description: The RFC 7662 endpoint. Must be absolute https, except to a loopback host.

client_id.description: Required: the client id presented to the introspection endpoint.

client_secret.description: The client secret written inline. Mutually exclusive with client_secret_env.

client_secret_env.description: The NAME of an environment variable holding the client secret. Mutually exclusive with client_secret; a named variable that is unset or empty fails the boot.

client_auth.description: How the client credentials are presented. Default basic.

token_type_hint.description: The optional RFC 7662 §2.1 token_type_hint parameter. Default access_token; set to "" to send no hint.

cache_ttl.description: Maximum lifetime of a cached verdict. Default 1m, capped at 15m.

negative_cache_ttl.description: How long a definitive refusal is remembered. Default 30s, capped at 15m.

http_timeout.description: Bounds a single introspection request. Default 5s.

proxyHeadersValidator.description: type: proxy_headers — an identity a fronting authenticating proxy already established, honoured only for peers inside the CIDR allowlist.

principal_claim.description: Accepted and ignored: there is no claim set here, only headers.

trusted_proxy_cidrs.description: Required and non-empty: the networks whose peers may assert an identity through headers. This allowlist IS the security model — never 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.

principal_header.description: Required: the header whose value becomes Principal.ID. No default is right for everyone.

tenant_header.description: Optional header whose value becomes Principal.Tenant.

scopes_header.description: Optional header whose value becomes Principal.Scopes, split on commas and/or whitespace.

stringOrStringList.description: A single string or a list of strings — both spellings the nexusauth/agui parsers accept.

duration.description: A Go duration string such as "10m", "30s" or "1h30m". A bare number is rejected on purpose: 600 reads as ten minutes to an operator and six hundred nanoseconds to Go.

artifacts.description: What a turn publishes as A2A Artifacts, and the caps that bound it. Tool results become artifacts unconditionally and files written during the turn ride inline as base64 raw parts, so without caps the store would grow with how chatty a turn was rather than with how many turns there were. Every cap DEGRADES rather than drops: an over-cap file becomes a metadata note naming it, over-cap tool output is truncated with a note, and a task that spends its budget publishes one notice saying how many artifacts it withheld. The store's worst case is max_task_bytes x tasks.max_per_context.

max_file_bytes.description: Largest file whose contents are inlined as a base64 raw part, in bytes. Default 262144 (256 KiB). A larger file degrades to a metadata note naming the file and its size. 0 means no file is ever inlined: every detected file becomes a note. Inline content is base64 in JSON, so it costs roughly a third more on the wire than on disk.

max_tool_output_bytes.description: Largest tool-result text carried on a tool-result artifact, in bytes. Default 16384 (16 KiB). Longer output is truncated on a rune boundary with a note saying how much was shown. 0 disables the cap.

max_task_bytes.description: One task's total artifact budget in bytes, counting every artifact except the final response. Default 1048576 (1 MiB). When it is spent, further artifacts are suppressed and one notice artifact records how many. 0 disables the budget, which makes the store's artifact growth unbounded.

file_base_dir.description: Directory that reported file paths are resolved against and confined to, expanded through engine.ExpandPath. Defaults to the session's files workspace, which is where nexus.tool.fileio writes unless an operator moved it. A reported path that escapes this directory (symlinks followed) is dropped, not clamped. With no session and no value set, file artifacts are disabled.

file_sources.description: Which structured-output keys of which tools carry the paths those tools wrote. Default {write_file: [path]}, matching nexus.tool.fileio. Setting this REPLACES the default wholesale. events.ToolResult.OutputFile is always honoured for every tool on top of this. Detection is tool.result-based by design: a write nothing reports is not published.
